_comment: Attack corpus for RF-03, shared by three levels of the test suite:
- engine/internal/rules/corpus_test.go   the rule chain, in isolation
- test/e2e/                              the live stack, through the proxy
A vector added here is therefore covered in all three at once. See
docs/testing-strategy.md for how to add one.
Fields are written exactly as they travel on the wire: 'query' is
percent-encoded the way a client would send it, because that is what both
Nginx hands the engine and what an HTTP client will transmit unchanged.
Several vectors are therefore only detectable after the engine decodes the
field, which is deliberate — it exercises the decode pass of scanTargets.
'signature' names the pattern that must fire. Signatures are evaluated in
file order per field, so each case here is written to reach its own
signature and no earlier one; a case that starts matching a different
signature is a real change in detection behaviour and should fail the test.

cases.description: q=x' UNION SELECT clave FROM usuarios-- — the classic column-stealing injection
id=1' OR '1'='1, fully percent-encoded — invisible until the engine decodes it
id=1; DROP TABLE usuarios — a second, destructive statement
usuario=admin'--&clave=x in a POST body — the case auth_request could never see (§1 of implementation-decisions.md)
id=1 AND sleep(5) — time-delay probe for blind injection
tabla=information_schema.tables — direct reference to the database catalogue
f=load_file('/etc/passwd') — SQL function reaching the host filesystem
A stored-XSS comment — the payload lives in the POST body
q= — breaking out of an inline script block

url=javascript:alert(1) — script URI in an attribute. Kept free of any other payload on purpose: an unencoded 'document.cookie' here would match cookie_theft against the raw field before the decode pass reaches this signature.
q= — inline event handler, no
q=<iframe src=//evil> — a tag that executes or redirects on its own
q=document.cookie — the DOM access of a session-stealing payload
url=data:text/html,... — HTML smuggled through a data: URI
Payload in the Referer header — proves headers are scanned, not just path, query and body
